title: adaptive-queue-economizer-and-capacity-curator
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds adaptive queueing-based burst control and a capacity curator service that recommends per-tenant reservation adjustments and exposes new telemetry for economic burst decisions.
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR introduces two related features aimed at improving Dedicated fleet economics and SLO stability under bursty workloads: an Adaptive Queue Economizer (AQE) in the serving path and a Capacity Curator service that synthesizes utilization signals to produce human-readable reservation recommendations. Customers on Dedicated were observing frequent microbursts that either violated latency SLOs or forced large over-reservations; existing slot-based autoscalers lacked short-term smoothing and a cost-aware admission knob. The AQE provides a transient, latency-aware backoff and fine-grained admission shaping at request-queue time; the Capacity Curator aggregates per-tenant telemetry to recommend commit/scale adjustments and flags tenants for manual review when cost/SLO tradeoffs become unfavorable.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introducing AQE middleware in the request router that computes a per-request admission score based on queue depth, recent tail latency percentiles (P95/P99), and tenant burst credits. The admission score gates requests into a fast-path/batched-path or defers them with a soft backoff window.
- New Capacity Curator microservice (stateless control loop) that consumes existing utilization rollups and the new AQE-derived burst_economizer_score metric to produce reservation guidance and a confidence score.
- Telemetry: new metrics exported via the observability pipeline: redwood.aqe.admission_rate, redwood.aqe.burst_economizer_score, redwood.curator.recommendation_delta, and redwood.curator.confidence. These are tagged per-tenant and per-pool.
- API: adds a read-only curator endpoint in the Console backend (/api/curator/v1/tenants/<tenant>/recommendation) and a preview panel in the Dedicated Console UI (backend + small TS client).
- Safety: curator recommendations are advisory only by default; an enterprise toggle (dedicated.curator.apply_recommendations=true) can be enabled via config for autopilot-style behavior.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- AQE is intentionally conservative: it never drops requests; it only delays or redirects them to slower, batched execution paths if latency risk is high. We designed the admission score to be monotonic with respect to queue depth and P99 latency so it is predictable under stress.
- Curator uses an exponential smoothing window (alpha=0.25 default) to avoid whipsaw recommendations. We considered a more aggressive predictive model but prioritized interpretability and safety for initial rollout.
- Cost-awareness: recommendations include both throughput and cost delta estimates (tokens/hour extrapolation). We avoided hard quotas to respect existing tenant SLAs; instead we provide deltas and a confidence band.

Checklist (what we tested):
- [x] Unit tests for AQE admission score logic (thresholding behavior, monotonicity).
- [x] Integration tests: simulated burst workload with synthetic tenants verifies reduced P99 tail and reduced peak reservation recommendations in curator simulator.
- [x] End-to-end smoke: Dedicated cluster staging run with a 12-hour soak; no regressions in throughput on steady-state workloads.
- [x] Telemetry validation: metrics ingest and dashboard panels render with expected labels.
- [x] Safety mode verified: curator.apply_recommendations=false results in read-only suggestions; enabling toggle applies delta via existing reservation API.

Commits (high-level):
- feat(aqe): add admission-score calculator and middleware hook
- feat(curator): new microservice skeleton and recommendation engine
- perf(router): fast-path routing for admitted requests (batching-friendly path)
- telemetry: add metrics and tagging in exporter and metric-enrichment layer
- ui: curator recommendation preview panel and API client

Changed areas / files (high-level):
- services/router/src/middleware/queue_economizer.go - core AQE logic (140 LOC)
- services/router/src/router/fast_path.go - fast-path admission and batching entrypoint (60 LOC)
- services/curator/* - new service (api, engine, tests)
- observability/exporter/metrics.go - metric definitions + tagging hooks
- console/backend/src/routes/curator.ts - read-only API proxy
- console/web/src/components/CuratorPreview.tsx - small TSX panel + tests
- infra/helm/dedicated/values.yaml - config toggle and default values

Small illustrative snippet (AQE admission score):
"""
// simplified pseudo-go
func computeAdmissionScore(qDepth int, p99 float64, credits float64) float64 {
    score := 1.0 + 0.05*float64(qDepth) + 0.8*(p99/targetP99) - 0.1*credits
    return clamp(score, 0.0, 1.0)
}
"""

Review conversation (selected):
- Liam Chen (reviewer): "Overall looks good. Can we avoid the extra allocation in the fast-path holder? I raised a comment on fast_path.go line 82. Also please add a short doc to design/ explaining the monotonicity invariants."
- Maya Patel (author): "Addressed: removed allocation by reusing pool buffer; added design doc with formal invariants and a few proof sketches. PTAL."
- Priya Kumar (reviewer): "Curator engine: please ensure the confidence calculation can't underflow for cold tenants — added suggestion to floor variance at 1e-6."
- Maya Patel: "Added floor and updated tests. Also added telemetry tag to indicate cold/steady tenants for easier dashboard filtering."
- Arjun Rao (approver): "Verified staging soak metrics and dashboard. Approving for merge after CI flake rerun."

CI summary:
- build (go): pass
- unit-tests (go): pass (coverage: router 84%, curator 76%)
- lint: pass (golangci-lint rules updated for new repo)
- e2e-staging (smoke): pass on second attempt (first run hit a flaky test unrelated to this change)

Migration / rollout notes:
- Default behavior: AQE enabled by default but with conservative thresholds; curator is deployed in read-only mode (recommendations only).
- Ops steps: we added Helm values under infra/helm/dedicated/values.yaml to tune alpha, admission thresholds, and the apply_recommendations toggle. Staged rollout recommended: enable AQE on low-traffic pools first, validate dashboards for 48 hours, then enable on more pools.
- Backout: removing the middleware is rollback-safe; curator is stateless and can be disabled via helm.

Observability and dashboards:
- New Grafana dashboard: Dedicated -> Queue Economizer (P95/P99, admission_rate, burst_economizer_score).
- Curator panel added to Tenant Overview with recommendation_delta and confidence.

Impact and metrics to watch post-merge:
- Expected P99 reduction for microburst tests: 20-40% depending on workload shape (simulator results).
- Expected reservation recommendation delta: -5% to -18% for tenants with transient microbursts (simulator median).
- Watch for increased request latency on batched-path (tradeoff) and admission_rate oscillations; we added alerts for admission_rate > 0.8 sustained for 5m.

Follow-ups (future work tracked in ENG-3511):
- Add a lightweight predictive component to curator to incorporate traffic trend forecasts.
- Experiment with a tenant-visible hint API so customers can opt-in to more aggressive econ-mode.
- Extend AQE admission signal to Dedicated control plane to influence autoscaler transient headroom allocation.

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash on 2026-02-18 after approvals from Arjun Rao and automated CI green. Release notes included above.

If you want to run locally:
- Router: make build-router && ./bin/router --config=./configs/dedicated-local.yaml
- Curator: make build-curator && ./bin/curator --sim-mode
